text:
maria.dev: heads up — nightly smokebench showed a p99 jump after the kernel-selector change merged last night. surfacing raw numbers now.

bench-bot: nightly-bench/attn-kernels #1851234560 completed: baseline p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=210ms -> new p50=19ms p95=76ms p99=295ms :warning:

aj: ouch, that's a noticeable tail shift. any single-run artifacts or consistent across GPUs?

maria.dev: ran on two A100 instances, both show same p99 lift. difference starts at sequence len ~1024 and above. small seqs look fine.

sam_w: do we have the exact harness command and kernel flags used? want to reproduce locally.

maria.dev: here are the args from the nightly job:
```
./bench_driver --model gptx-7b --kernel-selector v2 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seqlens 64,256,1024,2048 --iters 500 --pin-cpu --perf-mode
```

oliver: kernel-selector v2 did the heuristic fallback to fused-attn disabled when memory pressure high right? could expose more context switches.

kim: Also check whether kv-cache prefetch ordering changed. That can increase p99 if it causes async stalls.

aj: action items I'd suggest: 1) reproduce with a tight microbench for seq=1024/2048 single-batch and capturing perf counters, 2) run with --trace-kv and --trace-sched to see blocking, 3) compare output diffs to ensure correctness unaffected.

maria.dev: started microbench now (local devbox, same commit). dropping the iterations to 200 and enabling tracing.

bench-bot: job 1851234572 started (microbench-local).

sam_w: for perf counters, use:
```
perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses,mem-loads -r 5 ./bench_driver --model ... --seqlen 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200
```
This helps isolate if it's memory or compute bound.

oliver: also collect the runtime kernel selection log, example env: REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 to print chosen kernel per layer.

maria.dev: added REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG and --trace-kv. initial microbench run attached: p99=288ms, perf shows 2.1x cache-misses vs baseline.

kim: cache-miss spike suggests kernel variant is doing more indirect memory accesses (maybe different tiling). v2 selector might be choosing a kernel with poorer locality for long seqs.

aj: can we force the previous kernel path for a run to confirm? a simple A/B will prove causality.

maria.dev: yes, forcing kernel via env: REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fused-attn-v1. rerunning...

bench-bot: job 1851234620 completed: forced-fused run p99=212ms (close to baseline).

maria.dev: forced run p99 back to ~214ms. So selector choice is the likely cause.

sam_w: what's the selector decision rule for seq=1024? is it latency-model predicted or memory-based threshold?

oliver: current selector uses a mixed heuristic: if seq*batch > 2048 then pick kernel X else kernel Y, with a penalty term for estimated memory usage. Might be outdated for new fused implementation.

kim: can we add a safety delta when switching — i.e., prefer the kernel with lower p99 estimate for long sequences even if it costs a slight p50 increase? That maps to our SLOs.

aj: yes, propose selector change: add a tail-aware scoring function: score = alpha * p99_est + beta * p50_est + gamma * mem_penalty. default alpha > beta to prioritize tail. We should test with sweep alpha in {1,2,5}.

maria.dev: agreed. but before changing selector, let's hard-fail the heuristic that picks the new kernel for seq>=1024 until we add scoring. Make a short PR to gate v2 for long sequences.

sam_w: also need to update bench harness to include: seed control, perf counters, kernel debug, and an output-diff step comparing logits or sample tokens. Add small deterministic prompt set to catch correctness regressions.

maria.dev: proposed a tiny deterministic eval harness: 20 prompts, fixed RNG seed, compare top-5 logits per position. if any L_inf > 1e-4 flag as regression.

oliver: watch out: quantization/FP changes can produce small numeric diffs; threshold might need tuning per model/quant config. Keep it model-config aware.

kim: note for nightly: record full commit hash and docker image tag in bench metadata. reproducibility is key.

aj: I'll open two PRs: 1) selector safety gate for seq>=1024, 2) harness upgrades (seed, perf-counters, kernel debug, output-diff). I'll include example perf command and an automated report template.

maria.dev: thanks. timeline? this week would be nice since customers could hit long-seq tails.

aj: aiming to have PRs by EOD tomorrow, review Thursday.

bench-bot: labelling thread: bench-triage, kernel-selector, p99-regression.

sam_w: one more ask — add a small flamegraph capture (async-profiler) for the microbench so we can see scheduler jitter vs mem stalls.

maria.dev: noted, adding flamegraph step to the harness. will paste results when ready.

oliver: after fixes, let's run a controlled 24h soak on canary with both selectors and compare p99 distributions. if stable, roll selector update.

maria.dev: agreed. creating an ENG-RFC follow-up to document selector scoring and rollout plan.

kim: appreciated. small follow-up: add a short note in the console docs about which kernel is chosen and how to force older kernels for emergency rollbacks.

aj: good point. I'll add docs to the deploy runbook.

maria.dev: thanks team — will update here with microbench artifacts and PR links.

bench-bot: thread closed by bench-bot at 1851234899.
